mainTopic: The two versions of רבי נתן's report on 'הריני נזיר מן הגרוגרות', and the debate between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן over who taught that a barley מנחה pledge requires wheat.
overview: The גמרא first says our משנה does not match a ברייתא of רבי נתן, who reports the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל differently, and it gives two versions of his report. Next it brings a משנה from מנחות: someone who pledges a מנחה 'from barley' must bring one from wheat, while רבי שמעון exempts him. חזקיה says this follows בית שמאי, who hold a person to the first part of his words, as in the dried figs case. רבי יוחנן says instead that everyone agrees when the person explains that barley was a mistake. חזקיה adds that a pledge 'from lentils' creates nothing. The גמרא challenges him from בית שמאי, and answers that חזקיה retracted. רבא explains that the משנה's choice of barley over lentils made him understand בית שמאי like רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן, speaking within חזקיה's approach, argues that the retraction was not needed, because barley may be the bigger חידוש. This argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי נתן's report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה does not match a ברייתא in which רבי נתן reports the dispute differently: בית שמאי say he is both נדור and נזיר, and בית הלל say he is נדור but not a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says that בית שמאי rule he is bound by a vow and is also a נזיר. בית הלל rule he is bound by a vow but is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different תנא, רבי נתן, reports the dispute about 'הריני נזיר מן הגרוגרות' in a way our משנה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה only debates whether he is a נזיר. רבי נתן adds a second question: are the dried figs now forbidden by a vow (נדור)? According to him, both sides agree the figs are forbidden. They argue only about whether he is also a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: a teacher of the משנה period
as it is taught in a ברייתא
bound by a vow; here, the figs are forbidden to him
one who took the נזירות vow

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here: is he a נזיר, and are the figs forbidden by a vow? Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Natan says,
Beit Shammai say: he is bound by a vow, and he is a nazirite;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: נָדוּר וְאֵין נָזִיר.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: he is bound by a vow, but he is not a nazirite.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נתן, both sides agree he is נדור. בית שמאי add that he is also a נזיר, while בית הלל say he is not.

steps.title: Which opinions each side follows in the first version
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי combine רבי מאיר (he is a נזיר) with רבי יהודה (the figs are forbidden). בית הלל follow רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר and like רבי יהודה. בית הלל hold like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of רבי נתן's version by matching it to opinions already discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי מאיר, a person does not say words for nothing, so 'הריני נזיר' makes him a נזיר. Following רבי יהודה, the end of his statement also counts, so the figs become forbidden. בית הלל follow רבי יוסי, that a person is held to the end of his words, so only the figs are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a person does not say words for nothing
a person is held to the end of his words

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold
in accordance with Rabbi Meir and in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר explains why he is a נזיר, and רבי יהודה explains why the figs are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וּכְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first version, בית שמאי follow רבי מאיר together with רבי יהודה, and בית הלל follow רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A second version of רבי נתן's report
steps.stepSummary: In another version, בית שמאי say he is נדור but not a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is neither נדור nor a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רבי נתן says that בית שמאי rule he is bound by a vow but is not a נזיר. בית הלל rule he is neither bound by a vow nor a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way of quoting רבי נתן, in which both sides are more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now no one says he becomes a נזיר. The only argument is whether the figs become forbidden: בית שמאי say yes, and בית הלל say no.

phrases.english: Some say a different version:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says that Beit Shammai say:
he is bound by a vow, and he is not a nazirite;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: לֹא נָדוּר וְלֹא נָזִיר.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: he is not bound by a vow, and he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version of רבי נתן given in step 1 with a different one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, בית שמאי say he is נדור but not a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is neither.

steps.title: Which opinions each side follows in the second version
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי are like רבי יהודה, and בית הלל are like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא matches each side of the second version to an opinion already discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה explained that בית שמאי only meant the figs become forbidden by a vow. רבי שמעון holds that a pledge not made the way people normally pledge does not count at all, so nothing takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: an unusual pledge does not count at all

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי נתן. In the first, בית שמאי say נזיר and נדור, and בית הלל say only נדור. In the second, בית שמאי say only נדור, and בית הלל say nothing takes effect.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai are in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
and Beit Hillel are in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וּבֵית הִלֵּל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the second version in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The משנה in מנחות about pledging a מנחה the wrong way
steps.stepSummary: Someone who pledges a מנחה with a wrong detail must bring a proper one. רבי שמעון exempts him because he did not pledge the way people normally do.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one who says 'It is upon me to bring a מנחה from barley' must bring it from wheat. If he said 'from flour,' he must bring fine flour. If he said 'without oil and frankincense,' he must bring it with oil and frankincense. If he said 'half a tenth,' he must bring a full tenth. If he said 'a tenth and a half,' he must bring two. רבי שמעון exempts him, because he did not pledge the way people normally pledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source from מסכת מנחות with a similar pattern: a pledge with a detail that cannot work. It is setting up a question about who taught this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of his words, 'a מנחה upon me,' is binding. The impossible detail is corrected to the proper form. רבי שמעון disagrees and says the whole pledge falls away because it was not a normal way to pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned in a משנה elsewhere
a tenth of an איפה, the measure for a מנחה

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מנחות 103a.

phrases.english: One who says: "It is upon me to bring a meal-offering
from barley"
must bring from wheat.
If he said "flour," he must bring fine flour.
If he said "without oil and frankincense,"
he must bring it with oil and frankincense.
If he said "half a tenth," he must bring a full tenth.
If he said "a tenth and a half," he must bring two.
Rabbi Shimon exempts him,
as he did not donate in the manner of donors.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pledged מנחה with an improper detail is brought in its proper form. רבי שמעון exempts him entirely.

steps.title: Who taught that barley becomes wheat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that pledging a barley מנחה obligates a wheat one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who teaches that when someone says 'It is upon me to bring a מנחה from barley,' he brings it from wheat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion stands behind the first opinion in the מנחות משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling ignores the impossible detail and holds him to the first part of his words. The גמרא wants to know which known opinion works this way.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught that when one said:
"It is upon me to bring a meal-offering from barley,"
he brings it from wheat?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a barley pledge obligates a wheat מנחה.

steps.title: חזקיה: it is בית שמאי, as in the dried figs case
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the ruling is part of a dispute and follows בית שמאי. Just as they say the dried figs detail is ignored and he is a נזיר, here the barley detail is ignored and he brings wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: it is taught as a dispute, and it is בית שמאי. Don't בית שמאי say that when he said 'from dried figs and from fig cakes' he is a נזיר? So too, when he said 'from barley,' he brings from wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question by tying the מנחות ruling to בית שמאי in our נזיר משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold a person to the first part of his words, 'הריני נזיר' or 'a מנחה upon me,' and ignore the detail that does not fit. That is exactly the pattern of 'barley becomes wheat.' So that ruling is not agreed to by everyone; it is בית שמאי's side of a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who answers the question
it is taught as a dispute
a pressed cake of dried figs

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה links two cases with the same pattern: בית שמאי keep the first part of a vow and ignore a detail that does not fit, so the barley מנחה ruling follows בית שמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the first opinion in the מנחות משנה is not a plain, agreed rule. It depends on בית שמאי's approach in נזיר.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: It is taught as a dispute,
and it is Beit Shammai.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי כִּי אָמַר
phrases.english: Don't Beit Shammai say that when one said:
"I am a nazirite from dried figs and from fig cakes," he is a nazirite?
phrases.notes: This is the case of our משנה, even though only the end of his words is quoted here.

phrases.english: So too, when he said "from barley,"
he brings from wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: בְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת שְׁנוּיָה, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The barley-to-wheat ruling follows בית שמאי, who keep the first part of a vow and ignore a detail that does not fit, as in the dried figs case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees when he says he made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the barley מנחה ruling can fit everyone's view. It is talking about someone who later explains he did not know people cannot pledge that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say this ruling is everyone's opinion. The case is when he says: 'Had I known people don't pledge this way, I would not have pledged this way, but that way.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer from חזקיה to the question of who holds that a barley מנחה pledge requires a wheat one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה said the ruling follows only בית שמאי. רבי יוחנן says no, even בית הלל agree, because this person tells us that 'barley' was just a mistake. What he really wanted was a proper מנחה, so his pledge stands as a normal wheat מנחה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it is everyone's opinion,
in a case where he says: "Had I known
that people do not pledge this way,
I would not have pledged this way, but that way."
phrases.notes: He means: I would not have said barley; I would have said a normal wheat מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in step 6, different from חזקיה's answer in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling fits everyone's view, because the case is one where he explains that barley was a mistake and he really meant a proper מנחה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that pledging a barley מנחה requires a wheat one?

steps.title: חזקיה: Barley requires a wheat מנחה, but lentils mean nothing
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה limits the ruling. Pledging 'from barley' requires a wheat מנחה, but pledging 'from lentils' requires nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: They only taught this when he said 'from barley.' But if he said 'from lentils,' he brings nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה adds a limit to the ruling: it works for barley but not for lentils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some real מנחות are made from barley, so a person might honestly think a barley מנחה is allowed. No מנחה is ever made from lentils, so someone who says 'lentils' never meant a real מנחה, and nothing takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when; a limiting phrase

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said:
They only taught this when he said "from barley,"
but if he said "from lentils,"
he does not bring anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to חזקיה's view and adds a limit to the ruling about the barley מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pledge 'from barley' obligates a wheat מנחה. A pledge 'from lentils' obligates nothing.

steps.title: Lentils are like dried figs, so בית שמאי should make him bring a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חזקיה. He said the משנה follows בית שמאי, and בית שמאי make a person a נזיר even when he adds dried figs, which are just as far off as lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to whom does חזקיה explain the משנה? According to בית שמאי. But lentils for a מנחה are just like dried figs for a נזיר, and בית שמאי say he is a נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks חזקיה's lentil rule using his own claim that the משנה follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a נזיר has nothing to do with dried figs, just as everyone knows no מנחה is made of lentils. Still, בית שמאי say the person is a נזיר. So if the משנה follows בית שמאי, the lentil pledge should also require a wheat מנחה, which goes against what חזקיה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, consider; opens a line of reasoning
Explains it as following; sets it according to

phrases.english: Now, according to whom does Chizkiyah
explain the Mishnah?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about pledging a barley מנחה, from step 5.

phrases.english: According to Beis Shammai.
But lentils in relation to a mincha
are just like dried figs in relation to a nazir,
and Beis Shammai say he is a nazir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9 by combining it with חזקיה's earlier claim in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's rule that a lentil pledge means nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה follows בית שמאי, and בית שמאי make a person a נזיר even with the far-off detail of dried figs, then a far-off detail like lentils should also be ignored, and he should bring a wheat מנחה.

steps.title: חזקיה took back his first explanation
steps.stepSummary: The answer: חזקיה retracted. He no longer explains the barley משנה as following בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge simply: חזקיה changed his mind about his earlier explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What he took back is his claim from step 7 that the barley משנה follows only בית שמאי. Once that claim is gone, the comparison to dried figs no longer causes a problem for his lentil rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it back; he retracted

steps.confusionAlert: חזקיה did not take back his lentil rule. He took back his claim that the barley משנה follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Chizkiyah retracted from it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה explained the barley משנה as following בית שמאי only.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה gave up that explanation, so the dried figs comparison no longer works against his lentil rule.

steps.title: Why did חזקיה change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made חזקיה take back his earlier explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did he take it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind חזקיה's change of mind, and this sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a sage retracted is not enough. The גמרא wants to know what in the sources pushed him to change his view.

phrases.english: And why did he retract from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the retraction in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made חזקיה give up his explanation that the משנה follows בית שמאי?

steps.title: רבא: The משנה's choice of barley bothered him
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the wording of the משנה was a problem for חזקיה. If it followed בית שמאי, it should have taught the bigger new idea of lentils, not barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was difficult for him. Why does it teach specifically 'from barley'? Let it teach 'from lentils'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: the wording of the משנה itself showed חזקיה that his explanation was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי ignore even a far-off detail like dried figs, a משנה following them would teach the bigger new idea, that even 'lentils' requires a wheat מנחה. Since the משנה only mentions barley, it must not be following בית שמאי's ruling as חזקיה had understood it.

phrases.english: Rava said: The Mishnah was difficult for him:
Why does it specifically teach "from barley"?
Let it teach "from lentils"!
phrases.notes: Lentils would be the bigger חידוש, so the משנה would have picked that case if it meant it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה chose barley instead of the bigger case of lentils, so it cannot follow בית שמאי's ruling as חזקיה first understood it.

steps.title: חזקיה's new view: בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה now holds that בית שמאי's ruling about a נזיר follows רבי יהודה's approach. So it does not prove anything about a lentil מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, חזקיה holds: When בית שמאי ruled there, in the dried figs case, they meant it the way רבי יהודה explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's explanation by stating חזקיה's new understanding of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה no longer reads בית שמאי as ignoring the detail that does not fit. He now explains them like רבי יהודה: the person's words are given real meaning, so they create a vow that forbids the dried figs. A lentil מנחה has no possible meaning, so even בית שמאי would agree nothing takes effect, and the dried figs case no longer challenges חזקיה's lentil rule.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה keeps his lentil rule. He gave up saying the barley משנה follows בית שמאי, because בית שמאי's נזיר ruling works like רבי יהודה's view and does not apply to a meaningless lentil pledge.

phrases.english: Rather, Chizkiyah holds:
when Beis Shammai said it there,
phrases.notes: "There" is the נזיר case of dried figs.

phrases.english: it follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation from step 13 by stating חזקיה's new understanding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית שמאי's ruling about the נזיר follows רבי יהודה's view that his words have real meaning. A lentil מנחה has no meaning, so it creates nothing, and חזקיה's lentil rule stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even 'from lentils' he must bring a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that even if a person vows a מנחה 'from lentils,' he must still bring a proper wheat מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even if he said 'from lentils,' he must bring a proper מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's opinion. Even a vow of a מנחה 'from lentils' still obligates the person to bring a real wheat מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lentils are never used for any מנחה, so this is the hardest case. On its face, רבי יוחנן says the first words 'a מנחה is on me' still count. The next steps show this was not his own view: he said it within חזקיה's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Lentils. No מנחה is ever brought from them.
A flour offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even "from lentils."
phrases.notes: He means that even then, the person still has to bring a regular wheat מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִן הָעֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After חזקיה's retraction, the גמרא presents רבי יוחנן's contrasting view on lentils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a vow of a מנחה 'from lentils' obligates a proper wheat מנחה.

steps.title: Doesn't רבי יוחנן explain the משנה as a mistaken vower?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. He himself explained the barley משנה as a person who thought he could vow that way. That explanation cannot work for lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רבי יוחנן who said the משנה is a person who says: 'Had I known one can't vow this way, I would not have vowed this way but that way'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's own words. His explanation of the barley case does not fit lentils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן explained the barley משנה as an honest mistake: the person thought a barley מנחה was allowed. No one would think a lentil מנחה exists, so that reasoning should not apply to lentils. How, then, can רבי יוחנן obligate the lentil vower?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But isn't it Rabbi Yochanan who said,
[that the משנה is] where he says: "Had I known
that one does not vow this way,
I would not have vowed this way, but rather this way"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's statement in step 15 using his own earlier explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that even a lentil vow obligates a מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own reason, an honest mistake about what can be vowed, cannot apply to lentils, since nobody thinks a lentil מנחה exists.

steps.title: He said it only according to חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was not giving his own view. He was speaking according to חזקיה's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the words of חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The lentil ruling is not רבי יוחנן's own opinion. He was arguing within חזקיה's way of thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's real view stays the 'had I known' explanation. The lentil statement is a tool for challenging חזקיה, as the next lines show.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words, meaning according to his approach
The אמורא who first linked the משנה to בית שמאי

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן personally holds that a lentil vow obligates a מנחה. He is only saying what would follow from חזקיה's approach.

phrases.english: According to the words of Chizkiya
is what he said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the statement was made according to another's view, not the speaker's own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן personally rules that a lentil vow obligates a מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said it only to challenge חזקיה on חזקיה's own terms.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks חזקיה why he retracted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks חזקיה why he took back his בית שמאי explanation. He states the reason himself: because the משנה does not say 'from lentils.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You, what is your reason for retracting? Because the משנה does not teach 'from lentils.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן turns to חזקיה and names the reason for his retraction. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats רבא's explanation from step 13: a בית שמאי משנה should have taught the bigger case of lentils. רבי יוחנן lays out that reason clearly so he can knock it down.

phrases.english: You, what is the reason
that you retracted?
Because it does not teach "from lentils."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ מַאי טַעְמָא קָא הָדְרַתְּ בָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what 'according to חזקיה' means: רבי יוחנן now challenges חזקיה's retraction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did חזקיה retract his בית שמאי explanation?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the משנה mentions barley rather than lentils.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה means 'not only lentils, but even barley'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן pushes back. The משנה may be teaching in a 'not only this, but even that' style. Lentils are the obvious case for בית שמאי, and barley is the bigger חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is saying 'it is not necessary': it is not necessary to say that when he said 'from lentils' he brings a proper מנחה. There one can say he is backing out, and we hold him to his first words. But when he said 'from barley,' surely this is what he meant: 'If it is holy like the עומר מנחה...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues that the missing lentils are no proof. In fact, barley could be the harder case for בית שמאי. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With lentils, the person is clearly trying to back out of 'a מנחה is on me.' For בית שמאי, that makes it simple to hold him to his first words. With barley, he may truly mean a real barley offering like the עומר, so obligating a wheat מנחה is a bigger חידוש. That would explain why the משנה chose barley.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say: an 'obvious case, then bigger case' style of teaching
Hold him to his first statement
The עומר offering, a מנחה brought from barley

steps.whyThisMatters: If this holds, חזקיה had no good reason to retract. The משנה could still follow בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Perhaps he is speaking in the style of "it is not necessary":
It is not necessary [to say] when he said "from lentils,"
that he brings a proper meal-offering,
since one can say
that he is backing out [of his vow],
and [we] hold him to his first statement.
But when he said "from barley,"
surely this is what he is saying:
"If it is consecrated like the omer meal-offering,"
phrases.notes: The עומר offering was brought from barley. This sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason for retracting given in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה's wording, that barley instead of lentils shows it is not בית שמאי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes lentils are the bigger חידוש. Under a 'not only this, but even that' reading, barley is actually the bigger חידוש, because the barley vower may sincerely mean a real barley offering.
